stem: Regulation (Reg) E applies to what types of accounts?
why: Reg E is a consumer protection regulation covering consumer transactions: ATMs, POS debit cards, certain government benefit accounts, direct deposits, gift, payroll and prepaid cards, and foreign remittance transfers.

flashcard.front: Regulation (Reg) E applies to what types of accounts?
flashcard.back: Consumer accounts (it's a consumer protection regulation)

keyFact: Reg E: consumer accounts only

stem: What is the purpose of FDIC signage and advertising requirements?
options: To maintain public confidence in the banking system and show which products are FDIC-insured deposits
To advertise the bank's interest rates
To list the bank's branch hours
To meet the bank's CRA lending goals
why: The FDIC's mission includes maintaining stability and public confidence by insuring deposits. Non-deposit signage separates insured deposits from non-deposit products. Sign and advertising requirements date back to the Banking Act of 1935.

flashcard.front: What is the purpose of FDIC signage and advertising requirements?
flashcard.back: To comfort consumers: maintain public confidence and show which products are FDIC-insured deposits

keyFact: FDIC signs and advertising: maintain public confidence; separate insured deposits from non-deposit products

stem: Regulation (Reg) CC applies to what types of accounts?
why: Unlike many regulations, Reg CC applies to both consumer and commercial accounts. A classmate's guide words it as "all deposit accounts".

flashcard.front: Regulation (Reg) CC applies to what types of accounts?

keyFact: Reg CC: consumer AND commercial accounts

stem: In general, what does Regulation (Reg) CC allow?
options: Placing holds on deposited funds, within the funds-availability rules
why: Reg CC (Funds Availability) lets banks protect themselves from check fraud losses by placing holds on funds.

flashcard.front: In general, what does Regulation (Reg) CC allow?
flashcard.back: Placing holds on deposited funds (funds availability), e.g. to protect against check fraud

keyFact: Reg CC allows: holds on deposited funds

stem: Effective July 1, 2025, how much of a deposit of non-"next-day" checks must be made available the next day under Reg CC?
why: The next-day minimum availability amount rose from $225 to $275 effective July 1, 2025.
keyFact: Reg CC next-day minimum (eff. 7/1/2025): first $275 of non-next-day checks

stem: Banks had to update their Reg CC Funds Availability Disclosures for the new inflation-adjusted amounts by what date?
why: The new amounts took effect July 1, 2025, and the updated Funds Availability Disclosures were required by 7/31/25.
keyFact: Reg CC Funds Availability Disclosures updated by: 7/31/2025

stem: Under Reg CC, a Case by Case hold allows a bank to hold checks for how long?
why: Case by Case holds allow a 2 business day hold, and can be used with no reason given on the hold notice.
keyFact: Reg CC Case by Case hold: 2 business days

stem: A customer opened a checking account 12 days ago. Under Reg CC's new customer exception, the remaining amount from next-day items beyond the first $6,725 must be available by which business day?
why: For new customers (open less than 30 days), the remaining amount from next-day items must be available by the 9th business day.
keyFact: Reg CC new customer hold: up to 9 business days

stem: A customer deposits a $10,000 check. Using the Reg CC large deposit exception, what may the bank do?
options: Make the first $6,725 available per its policy and hold the rest up to 7 business days
Make the first $5,525 available per its policy and hold the rest up to 7 business days
Make the first $6,725 available per its policy and hold the rest up to 9 business days
Hold the entire $10,000 for up to 7 business days with no amount released
why: Deposits greater than $6,725 qualify; the first $6,725 follows the availability policy (usually next day) and the remainder can be held up to 7 business days.
keyFact: Reg CC large deposit exception: over $6,725 (eff. 7/1/2025); remainder held up to 7 business days

stem: For Reg CC's new customer exception, a customer is considered new if the account has been open for less than how long?
why: The New Customers exception applies to accounts open for less than 30 days.
keyFact: Reg CC new customer: account open less than 30 days

stem: If a bank's reason for doubting a check's collectibility is confidential, it must state that fact on the hold notice and document the confidential reason in its records.
why: The reason for the belief normally goes on the customer's notice; if it's confidential, the bank states that fact on the notice and documents the reason in its records.

stem: Under Reg CC, an account can be considered repeatedly overdrawn if, on two or more banking days during the previous six months, its balance was negative by $6,725 or more.
why: That is one of the two tests. The other is a negative balance of any amount on six or more banking days during the previous six months.
keyFact: Reg CC repeatedly overdrawn: 6+ negative days in 6 months, or 2+ days negative $6,725 or more

stem: Which of these may NOT be used as the basis for a Reg CC hold for reasonable cause to doubt collectibility?
options: The check is of a particular class or deposited by a particular class of person
The check is postdated or dated more than six months earlier
The paying institution has said it will not honor the check
Facts giving a reasonable person a well-grounded belief the check is uncollectible
why: The belief that a check is uncollectible shall NOT be based on the check being of a particular class or deposited by a particular class of person.

stem: A Reg CC hold decided after the deposit was made, or on a deposit not made in person, must be disclosed to the customer no later than when?
options: The first business day after the deposit
The same day the deposit is made
The second business day after the deposit
The seventh business day after the deposit
why: Holds are disclosed at the time of deposit unless the deposit isn't made in person or the decision comes after the deposit; then no later than the first business day after deposit.
keyFact: Reg CC hold notice (not in person or decided later): by the first business day after deposit

stem: The FDIC delayed the mandatory compliance date for 12 CFR 328.4 and 328.5 (digital channels and ATMs) to what date?
why: The December 2023 final rule had a mandatory compliance date of May 1, 2025, but 328.4 and 328.5 were delayed to April 1, 2027.
keyFact: FDIC 328.4 and 328.5 (digital and ATM signs): April 1, 2027

stem: What colors is the new FDIC official digital sign for bank websites, apps, and ATMs?
why: The traditional physical official sign is black and gold; the new official digital sign is navy blue and black.
keyFact: FDIC official digital sign: navy blue and black (physical sign is black and gold)

stem: The FDIC says the official digital sign can even be placed in a page's footer, as long as its placement is still clear, continuous, and conspicuous.
why: The FDIC's placement examples are not absolute mandates; the sign can be in the footer if it stays clear, continuous, and conspicuous.

stem: A bank's ordinary homepage automatically needs the non-deposit disclosure if it has an "Investments" or "Wealth Management" link.
why: The requirement focuses on pages primarily dedicated to non-deposit products. A homepage doesn't need it merely because it has an Investments link.

stem: An ATM placed in service after April 1, 2027 lets customers transact with non-deposit products. What FDIC signage does it need?
options: The FDIC digital sign on the initial screen
A physical FDIC sign in place of the digital sign
No FDIC sign, only the non-deposit disclosure
The FDIC digital sign on the printed receipt
why: An ATM placed in service after 4/1/2027 that permits non-deposit transactions requires the FDIC digital sign on the initial screen.

stem: Under Reg E, a bank may wait to begin investigating an unauthorized EFT until the consumer files a police report or disputes the charge with the merchant.
why: The Official Staff Commentary states an institution may not delay its investigation pending receipt of information from the consumer.

stem: When the alleged error is an unauthorized EFT, the burden of proof is on the consumer to show the transaction was not authorized.
why: The EFTA places the burden of proof on the financial institution to establish that the transaction was authorized.

stem: Generally, a bank must finish a Reg E error investigation within how long of receiving the error notice?
why: The general rule is 10 business days; it can be extended to 45 calendar days if conditions are met, and in certain cases to 90 days.
keyFact: Reg E investigation: 10 business days, extendable to 45 calendar days (90 in certain cases)

stem: To extend a Reg E investigation to 45 calendar days, the bank must tell the consumer the amount and date of the provisional credit within how long of the crediting?
why: The bank must provisionally credit within 10 business days, inform the consumer within two business days of crediting, and allow full use of the funds.
keyFact: Reg E provisional credit notice: within 2 business days of crediting

stem: Which of these errors qualifies for extending a Reg E investigation from 45 to 90 days?
options: One that resulted from a point-of-sale debit card transaction
One that involved a withdrawal at the bank's own ATM
One that occurred within 60 days after the account was opened
One that involved a domestic online bill payment
why: The 90-day extension covers foreign-initiated EFTs, point-of-sale debit card transactions, and errors within 30 calendar days after the first deposit into the account.
keyFact: Reg E 90-day extension: foreign-initiated, POS debit, or within 30 days of first deposit

stem: After completing a Reg E investigation, the bank must report the results to the consumer within three business days.
why: The bank must correct an error within one business day of determining it occurred and report the results within three business days after completing the investigation.
keyFact: Reg E after investigation: correct within 1 business day; report within 3 business days

stem: When a bank debits a Reg E provisional credit after finding no error, for how long must it honor the consumer's checks and preauthorized transfers without charging overdraft fees?
options: Five business days after the notification
Two business days after the notification
Ten business days after the notification
Three business days after the notification
why: The bank honors those items without overdraft fees for five business days after the notification, if they would have been paid had the provisional credit not been debited.
keyFact: Reg E debit of provisional credit: honor items without OD fees for 5 business days

stem: A consumer reports a stolen debit card one business day after learning of the theft. What is the consumer's maximum liability under Reg E?
options: The lesser of $50 or the total unauthorized transfers
The lesser of $500 or the total unauthorized transfers
Unlimited liability until the bank is notified
why: Notice within two business days after learning of the loss or theft caps liability at the lesser of $50 or the total amount of unauthorized transfers.
keyFact: Reg E lost card, notice within 2 business days: lesser of $50 or total

stem: A consumer reports a lost debit card five business days after learning of the loss, well within 60 days of the statement. What is the consumer's maximum liability?
why: Notice after two business days but within 60 calendar days of the statement caps liability at the lesser of $500 or the sum of the first-two-day amount (up to $50) plus later transfers before notice.
keyFact: Reg E lost card, notice after 2 business days (within 60 days): up to $500

stem: An unauthorized transfer that did NOT involve a lost or stolen access device is reported within 60 calendar days after the statement on which it first appears. What is the consumer's liability?
options: The lesser of $50 or the total
The lesser of $500 or the total
why: Unauthorized transfers not involving loss or theft of an access device reported within 60 calendar days of the statement carry no consumer liability.
keyFact: Reg E no lost device, notice within 60 days of statement: no liability

stem: In July 2025, the OCC, Federal Reserve Board, and FDIC rescinded the 2023 CRA final rule and replaced it with the prior CRA regulations originally adopted in what year?
why: The agencies went back to the CRA regulations originally adopted in 1995, with certain technical amendments.
keyFact: CRA July 2025: 2023 rule rescinded; back to the 1995 regulations

stem: For 2026, a small bank under the existing CRA framework has assets of less than what amount as of December 31 of either of the prior two calendar years?
why: The 2026 small bank threshold is less than $1.649 billion, up from $1.609 billion in 2025. The $1 billion and $10 billion figures are only in the OCC/FDIC proposal.
keyFact: CRA 2026 small bank: less than $1.649 billion

stem: For 2026, what is the lower asset threshold for an intermediate small bank under the existing CRA framework?
why: An intermediate small bank has at least $412 million as of December 31 of both prior calendar years. The 2025 lower threshold was $402 million.
keyFact: CRA 2026 intermediate small bank: at least $412 million

stem: The proposed CRA categories of small bank (under $1 billion), intermediate bank ($1 to $10 billion), and large bank (over $10 billion) are currently in effect.
why: Those categories are only in the OCC/FDIC proposal and are not currently effective. Banks should use the current 2026 $412 million/$1.649 billion thresholds and not implement the proposal yet.

stem: Under the current status of Section 1033 open banking, the April 2026 compliance deadline is enforceable and banks can stop monitoring the rule.
why: The April 2026 deadline is not currently enforceable, the original 2024 rule is under reconsideration, and banks should not stop monitoring.
